top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers and four valves of the human heart.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the heart.
Explain the functional differences between the right and left ventricles.
Describe the role of the heart valves in preventing backflow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the overall structure and major vessels of the heart.
key_visuals: Anatomically accurate 3D model of the human heart, exterior view
Labels for the superior and inferior vena cava, aorta, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary veins
student_actions: Rotate and zoom the heart model to view it from all angles.
Tap on each major vessel to see its name and a brief description.

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify and differentiate the four chambers of the heart.
key_visuals: 3D model of the heart with major vessels removed to reveal the interior
Clearly demarcated and labeled right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle
Visual cues highlighting the relative thickness of the ventricular walls
student_actions: Compare the thickness of the left and right ventricular walls.
Read information about the function of each chamber.

scenes.brief_purpose: Locate and identify the four heart valves.
key_visuals: 3D model of the heart showing the internal chambers and valves
The four valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic) clearly visible and labeled
Animation showing the open and closed states of each valve
student_actions: Locate each of the four valves within the heart model.
Observe the valve animations to understand their function in controlling blood flow.
Tap on each valve to learn its name and function.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body to the lungs.
key_visuals: 3D heart model with a highlighted path and animated flow of blue "deoxygenated" blood
Arrows indicating the direction of blood flow
Labels for the vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries
student_actions: Initiate an animation showing deoxygenated blood entering the right atrium.
Follow the blood as it moves through the right side of the heart and into the pulmonary arteries.
Pause the animation at key points to review the structures involved.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs to the body.
key_visuals: 3D heart model with a highlighted path and animated flow of red "oxygenated" blood
Arrows indicating the direction of blood flow
Labels for the pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta
student_actions: Initiate an animation showing oxygenated blood entering the left atrium via the pulmonary veins.
Follow the blood as it moves through the left side of the heart and into the aorta.
Observe how the left ventricle's contraction pumps blood to the rest of the body.

scenes.brief_purpose: Combine the pathways to illustrate the complete cardiac cycle and dual-loop circulation.
key_visuals: Animated 3D heart model showing simultaneous flow of both deoxygenated (blue) and oxygenated (red) blood
A simplified representation of the pulmonary and systemic circuits
Visual emphasis on the coordinated action of the chambers and valves
student_actions: Observe the complete, continuous circulation of blood through the heart and body.
Relate the thicker left ventricular wall to the higher pressure needed for systemic circulation.
Answer review questions about the entire process.
